page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with an Intel Xeon 8163 processor containing 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The system features 31.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.88 GB per core. Graphics and parallel computing acceleration are provided by a single NVIDIA T4 GPU based on the Turing architecture, which includes 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. This instance does not include local storage and relies on network-attached storage, supported by a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a clear distinction between CPU-bound and GPU-accelerated performance. General CPU performance is modest, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core metrics falling into the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, along with software compilation and ray tracing tests, rank in the lower 25% bracket. Memory bandwidth shows average performance for large uncached blocks at approximately 39.4 GB/sec for read operations, but drops to the bottom 25% for small cached blocks.

In contrast to the CPU limitations, the integrated NVIDIA T4 GPU delivers strong performance in machine learning tasks. LLM inference benchmarks show top-tier prompt processing speeds, reaching over 8,407 tokens per second for a small 135M model and 1,134 tokens per second for a medium 7B model. Text generation speeds are average for the 135M model but remain strong for the 7B model at 33.96 tokens per second. Consequently, this server is highly cost-efficient for specialized workloads such as low-latency model inference, small-scale AI deployment, and GPU-accelerated parallel processing, while being less optimal for general-purpose CPU computing or high-throughput local storage operations.
